title: New class polar-active-fluid (Toner-Tu flocks that eat), negative: self-propulsion turns Gray-Scott splitting spots into travelling fronts and bands, not motile individuals, in every one of 15 settings
summary: world.py is a Toner-Tu density-polarization continuum (self-advection v0 rho p, ordering above rho_c with |p| <= 1, pressure w grad rho) whose agents grow autocatalytically on a diffusing, regrowing food (k c rho^2, Gray-Scott kinetics) and die at d. With v0=0 it is Gray-Scott: from noise, 160 still spots that split (58 and 62 persistent splits, generation 3, seeds 0 and 1). With v0 0.25 the first crescents (t~120, pack/seed0/sheet.png) move into fresh food, their flanks keep growing, and within ~400 t every flock has become a front; the fronts align into travelling bands that span the box (3-4 components at t=3000, 0 persistent splits). A 14-setting screen (scan/SCAN.md: speed 0.1-1, food diffusivity 0.16-1, kill rate, self-advection lam 0.8-2, alignment 0.2-1, and a speed that rises with density so thin flanks lag) gives bands, chaotic fronts, or extinction; never finite flocks.

finding.operator: Toner-Tu polar self-propulsion (v0 rho p, ordering above a critical density) added to autocatalytic growth on a consumed, regrowing food
finding.control: matched v0=0 twin (pack_v0, seeds 0 1) and a 14-setting screen
finding.result: v0=0: 166/163 spots, 58/62 persistent splits, generation 3; v0=0.25: 4/3 components (box-spanning bands), 0 persistent splits, 0 persistent tracks; density-dependent speed with lam 2 (pack_rs): 15 chaotic front pieces, 0 persistent splits, 966 nucleations

limits: One grid (128^2, dx 1) and one time step (0.25, explicit upwind advection). The front instability is generic for an eater moving into fresh food: a moving flock's flanks also meet fresh food and grow, and nothing in a polar fluid pulls them back (in c49's reacting thermals the vortex pair curls the flanks into arms that break off). Untried routes that might bound the flanks: a nematic or chiral (rotating p) term, a density-dependent alignment that turns the flanks inward, a conserved number of agents instead of growth, or a long-range repellent. Early crescents (t~100-200) are real but transient.
